command: llvm-mc -triple=aarch64 -filetype=obj A64-P23-adr-imm21.s -o out.o && llvm-objcopy -O binary --only-section=.text out.o out.bin
notes: Input (LF, trailing newline) is `research/evidence/experiments/EXP-0117/A64-P23-adr-imm21.s`: label `back` at 0, five literal displacements (`#0`, `#8`, `#-8`, `#1048575`, `#-1048576`), label `ahead` at 20, then `adr x5, ahead` at 20, `adr x6, back` at 24 and `adr x7, ahead` at 28. The last three rows are symbol sites that this assembler resolves itself, so `llvm-readobj -r` is empty and no linker is involved; the plan states the same three displacements through `pcrel_begin` + `identity`. Measured words: `10000000`, `10000041`, `10ffffc2`, `707fffe3`, `10800004`, `10000005`, `10ffff46`, `10ffffc7`. Bit 31 is 0 (`adr`; `adrp` sets it), `immlo` holds the low two bits of the signed 21-bit byte displacement at 29-30 and `immhi` bits 2-20 at 5-23. `llvm-objdump -d` prints the target as `P + v` and wraps at 64 bits, so `adr x4, #-1048576` disassembles as `0xfffffffffff00010` while `adr x3, #1048575` is `0x10000b`; both readings agree with the derivation in `measure.py`. `adr x0, #1048576` is one past the range and `llvm-mc` rejects it (`expected label or encodable integer pc offset`).
